body_md: For $n=0, 1$ conditions $(2)$ and $(3)$ do not make sense.  By convention an $A_0$-comonoid object is a zero object, and an $A_1$-comonoid object is simply an object of $\mathcal{C}$. The second condition is dual to the usual Segal condition for a monoid, the third condition says that the comultiplication induced by the Segal conditions is counital. title: Proof
body_md: Consider a chain of inclusions $[m_0]\xrightarrow{f_1}[m_1]\xrightarrow{f_2}\dots\xrightarrow{f_k}[m_k]$ in $\Delta_n$ which does not belong to $\Delta_n^0$. We want to show that such a $k$-simplex lifts to one in $\square[n+1]_0$. Necessarily $[m_k] = [n]$.  The lift is given by the image of the chain of inclusions $J_0 \subseteq J_1 \subseteq \dots\subseteq [n]$ where $J_i = im(f_k\circ\cdots\circ f_{i+1})$.  This is similar to the proof of \cite[Proposition 4.1.5.7]{HA}.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{sconodata}
The functor $Fun^{sco}(\square[n], \mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{C}^n$ given by pulling back along the inclusion of cardinality one subsets of $[n]$ is an equivalence.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: There is a fully faithful left Kan extension functor \[Fun(P_{\le1}(\{0,\dots,n-1\}, \mathcal{C})\hookrightarrow Fun(\square[n], \mathcal{C})\] from diagrams defined on subsets of $[n-1]$ of cardinality less than two to diagrams defined on the entire powerset of $[n-1]$.  $Fun^{sco}(\square[n], \mathcal{C})$ can be identified with the image of this functor on the subcategory of $Fun(P_{\le1}(\{0,\dots,n-1\}, \mathcal{C})$ of diagrams with initial vertex a 0 object.  This category is equivalent to $\mathcal{C}^n$.

title: Definition
body_md:
(Heuts)
An $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$ is \textit{$n$-excisive} if every weak $n$-excisive approximation to $\mathcal{D}$ is an equivalence. An adjunction $F:\mathcal{C}\rightleftarrows \mathcal{D}:G$ is an $n$-excisive approximation to $\mathcal{C}$ if it is a weak $n$-excisive approximation and the $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$ is $n$-excisive.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md: An $\infty$-category is $1$-excisive if and only if it is stable. The $1$-excisive approximation to $\mathcal{S}_\star$, the $\infty$-category of pointed spaces, is the usual stabilization adjunction $\Sigma^\infty:\mathcal{S}_\star\rightleftarrows Sp:\Omega^\infty$.

title: Proof
body_md:
There is an equivalence  
\[Fun(\Delta_n, \mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{\sim} lim_k Fun(\Delta_n, \mathcal{C}_k) \]
which we must show lifts to an equivalence 
\[coMon_n(\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{\sim} lim_k coMon_n(C_k) \]

title: Lemma
body_md: Suppose the comparison functor $\mathcal{C}\rightarrow P_\infty(\mathcal{C})$ is an equivalence, then the functor  $\hat{P}_\infty\mathcal{C} \rightarrow P_\infty\mathcal{C}$ is an equivalence.

title: Proof
body_md: If $\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{\sim} P_\infty(\mathcal{C})$ is an equivalence then $\Sigma:\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{\sim} coGrp_\infty(\mathcal{C})$ is an equivalence by Theorem \ref{limit} and so $\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{\sim}\hat{P}_\infty\mathcal{C}$ is an equivalence.  The result then follows by the two out of three property for equivalences.
